And what sets it apart is the steel heart inside the dial which “beats” once a second as its two halves separate and then reunite, driven by a patented device. The secret is an innovative quartz movement, designed and manufactured exclusively for Salvatore Ferragamo. Pressing the crown starts the function, while the time is set with a button at 2 o’clock using a special heart-shaped tool. It truly is a special and mesmerising object and I have managed to fascinate everybody I know closely with my Cuore Ferragamo and it’s beating heart. I’m in LOVE! I went for a classic black calfskin strap and I love the fact that the women’s dial is not as tiny as they usually are in other brands – I have always been a fan of large dials which is why I’m more fond of men’s watches than women’s, but the Cuore Ferragamo has a really perfect dial size which is not too small, not too big, magnificently heavy/solid and completely classy.Cuore Ferragamo is available with a bi-colour bracelet or a crocodile print calfskin strap in one of a sophisticated palette of colour shades: yellow, black, red, purple, pink and grey. Here is a lovely video to show you the true beauty of the Cuore Ferragamo and how exactly the heart beats:And now onto all the pics to show you the Agra experience. On the road. It’s been quite some time since we were whisked away to a beautiful stay in Agra by Salvatore Ferragamo for the launch of their lovely new ‘Cuore‘ watch in India and I had some lovely pics of the experience that I HAD to share with you. Our stay was arranged at the brilliant Oberoi Amarvilas, which was also the venue for the official launch event followed by a gala dinner and I have photographs of it all (lots of them so have fun browsing!)We started off with a road trip to the hotel in Agra where we were treated to immaculate hospitality and spectacular views of the Taj Mahal right from our room, where we rested and got ready for the exciting evening. The Cuore watch has been created by Salvatore Ferragamo as a perfect accessory and an ideal gift of love for a special occasion like an anniversary or even the birthday of a loved one. And what sets it apart is the steel heart inside the dial which “beats” once a second as its two halves separate and then reunite, driven by a patented device. The secret is an innovative quartz movement, designed and manufactured exclusively for Salvatore Ferragamo. Pressing the crown starts the function, while the time is set with a button at 2 o’clock using a special heart-shaped tool. It truly is a special and mesmerising object and I have managed to fascinate everybody I know closely with my Cuore Ferragamo and it’s beating heart. I’m in LOVE! So when it does, my suggestion is to buy that pair of jeans and buy it HARD. Maybe even 2 pieces of the same thing (yes, I’ve done that myself)And when I heard of the Sculpted Jeans by Calvin Klein Jeans, I was intrigued to go and try them on. Probably something to do with the ‘Sculpted’ term in the name being used – ingenious! I visited the Calvin Klein store in Select Citywalk Mall, New Delhi to try out a pair for myself. I was looking for something classic that I’ll be able to wear in a heartbeat. So I went for the classic blue denim. And I fell in love. It’s a perfect not too high waist, not too low waist so it sits perfectly on your waist and the fit is a dream. The jeans really do sculpt around your ass and make it look so good. Or maybe I just love my ass more than usual lol! No camel-toes and just an all-round great fit on the body. Simple and good.Since I was already there, I also decided to try out the new Calvin Klein Seamless Logo Bra – a seamless, smooth bra that’s quite like liquid in the way it moves. This would be perfect under basic tees and even by themselves! And that color is such a nice pop!I am wearing a total Calvin Klein look here, shirt is from the menswear section because if you know me well enough by now you’ll know that this is what I usually go for, a logo belt because it looked so good with just a white shirt and blue jeans. And a comfy bag. Hope you enjoy the pics. While you’re walking around, you almost always get stopped by someone who either wants to take a pic of your outfit or a detail of your outfit, or a quick byte on some designer’s collection, or a boomerang video or a full on interview.      And because I end up being in front of the camera a lot, I make it a point to check if my make is point, needs any retouching or not. Nothing major but mainly either retouching my lipstick or blotting the extra oil off the skin. The selfie camera (without the beautification filter)  on the Notepad 5 acts as my mirror wherever I go. No need to make a trip to the washrooms just to get access to a mirror.      Et voila! All along my two most important accessories are my camera and my smartphone and this time I have partnered with Coolpad India to get me through #AIFWSS17 with their new smartphone – Coolpad Note 5. So here goes.                  I usually arrive during late afternoon when there are fewer people and the day is still a bit sluggish. This gives me time and space to do do my ourtit shoot which I share with you daily throughout Fashion Week. A different look each day.      Sometimes you end up making a new friend during the shoot too.      By the time I’m done with my shoot the pace for the day has picked up. There are lot more people and the general buzz and energy levels of the venue have gone up. Since fashion week is such a hotspot for the fashion & textile industry related professionals, I am always running into friends, acquaintances, clients and PR professionals and it’s almost a mandate to take a selfie after you have said hello. It’s kinda like the new handshake but somehow not as polished as a handshake. But you still gotta do it.Saying hello to Rasna Bhasin – influencer and at Bazaar Bride      The selfie from the Coolpad Note 5      Saying hello to Pranav & Shyma – the designers at Huemn      The selfie from the Coolpad Note 5      Then I usually attend a few runway shows from the day. Here I’m seated for the Mandira Wirk show and well it’s time to take another selfie. It’s quite dark inside the show area so having a led flash for your selfie camera inbuilt in the smartphone itself is GODSENT! You can adjust the distance of the camera from your face to decide how strong you want the flash light to be because it’s continuously on like a torch (it doesn’t just go off when the pic is being clicked) – another plus.      After the show, I head over to Mandira Wirk’s stall at the venue to get a closer look at her collection. It’s always a good idea to get a touch & feel of the collection, see the details and embellishments and truly get a chance to appreciate all the work that has gone in.      If you manage to find time, you grab a bite, reply to some emails (thank you for the open WiFi this time!) and make a few important phone calls.      While you’re walking around, you almost always get stopped by someone who either wants to take a pic of your outfit or a detail of your outfit, or a quick byte on some designer’s collection, or a boomerang video or a full on interview.      And because I end up being in front of the camera a lot, I make it a point to check if my make is point, needs any retouching or not. Nothing major but mainly either retouching my lipstick or blotting the extra oil off the skin. The selfie camera (without the beautification filter)  on the Notepad 5 acts as my mirror wherever I go. No need to make a trip to the washrooms just to get access to a mirror.      Et voila! Perfect Red Lips.      Before you know it the sun has disappeared, it’s dark and the lights have come on everywhere making everything look so much more magical and festive! They had installed this huge AIFW bulb sign right at the entry to the venue and it instantly became one of the most clicked objects during the #AIFWSS17 this time. And it looks so much better at night with the lights on! Had to get a selfie with it too!            A few shows more perhaps and it’s time to call it a day. In the past I used to do a lot more during fashion week – pre-show parties, after parties and a lot more shows! And can’t quite comprehend where I managed to create that kind of energy and willpower. But now it’s a lot more about work for me. So once I know I have my content for the day, It’s time for me to head back home, start editing photographs, content, drafting blog posts. reshare social media posts in which I have been featured and also have dinner (most important). It sounds a bit non-glamorous and maybe it even is, but it’s real, it’s work, it’s fun and it makes me money! Not to mention, it allows to get my beauty sleep  So cheers to everyone who is a part of the fashion industry! And see you next season!      A big thank you to Coolpad for letting me experience the Notepad 5 during the Fashion Week and really put it to test. It’s most impressive because after ALL of this above and more, the device has enough juice left right till the time I go to sleep after wrapping up everything for the day. Which means I did not have to carry a powerbank on a single day of fashion week and those things can sometimes get too big or heavy for the tiny bags I have picked out for my looks. This dress is from the Autumn Winter Collection and is in stores now. It’s perfect for the Winter transition, sleeveless and short but still keeps you a bit warm because of the pvc. Great for evenings with some pretty earrings (Dior in this case) and a classic black bag (also from Benetton). A smokey eye would go really well with this whole outfit but since I wore it in the day I didn’t want to go too serious with my makeup. But nude lips for a change since I rarely ever go for nude lips. What do you think? Well, atleast a statement on a tee! ‘Not A Fashion Victim’. I’m not really sure why term term ‘Fashion Victim’ even exists in the first place. Being such a personal choice, fashion can never really have victims. As long as you are comfortable and confident in what you’re wearing. Yes perhaps it was coined for people who fall victim to following trends (whatever that even means anymore) even if it doesn’t suit them or makes them feel unnatural. This tee is for the people who love fashion, even if they don’t know why, aren’t afraid to try new things and those who certainly don’t give two bat shits about what somebody else will think about their outfit. With Naina.                         Ending the Amazon India Fashion Week Spring Summer 2017 with a statement. Well, atleast a statement on a tee! ‘Not A Fashion Victim’. I’m not really sure why term term ‘Fashion Victim’ even exists in the first place. Being such a personal choice, fashion can never really have victims. As long as you are comfortable and confident in what you’re wearing. Yes perhaps it was coined for people who fall victim to following trends (whatever that even means anymore) even if it doesn’t suit them or makes them feel unnatural. This tee is for the people who love fashion, even if they don’t know why, aren’t afraid to try new things and those who certainly don’t give two bat shits about what somebody else will think about their outfit. Love yourself and embrace yourself. It exists to please you, not make a mockery out of you – Fashion.My look is again so simple with just a cute little black skirt that would give my tee all the attention it needs, with black and white sneakers from Day 03 and an #IndiaModernFestive element of chandbalis to make you suddenly go ‘wait what?!’This has been a great season and I’m already looking forward to the next one. Tomorrow I leave for a exciting trip to Geneva & Milan with Glion Institute of Higher Education! They have a bunch of exciting experiences that await me along with a few other bloggers from different parts of the world. I will be gone for 10 days and I have no time to pack or even gather my thoughts. It’s busy, it’s hectic, it drives me crazy but at the end of the day I LOVE what I do and I wouldn’t have it any other way! There is a lot more stuff coming on the blog coming week so stay tuned! Till next season, it’s a wrap with the Amazon India Fashion Week!                                                                  The last selfie I took for #AIFWSS17. (woooooh!) and also despair because it’s only going to come back after 6-12 months for me (depending on whether I’m in town for next season). Today for Day 03 of Amazon India Fashion Week SS17, I went for an ‘evergreen’ style in my books – a long shirt dress over a mini dress underneath – you can keep either one a solid color and the other one printed. I still have to try pairing both printed together which isn’t a total crime (I’m sure it can be done). That’s the most amazing thing about fashion – it’s personal. Coz it was Day 02 of the Amazon India Fashion Week SS17 and you kinda need that sugar rush to keep you going (or maybe an espresso shot. Or 10). I just had the worse timing of getting two of my teeth extracted (one normal and one wisdom) just 2 days before the #AIFWSS17 was to start. Now I’m left with stitches in my mouth, and the look of a total grumpy face because I can’t smile properly or even talk too much – no food or alcohol can also be consumed either (only soft and cold foods and a diet of antibiotics and painkillers). But it was one those things that I had been delaying for over 8 months and if I hadn’t gotten it done when I did, I would have had to suffer another 8 because I just cannot get myself to visit a dentist. So if you see me at Fashion Week and I don’t smile back at you or smile really weird, you’ll know why.Candy candy candy! Candy candy candy! Coz it was Day 02 of the Amazon India Fashion Week SS17 and you kinda need that sugar rush to keep you going (or maybe an espresso shot. Or 10). I just had the worse timing of getting two of my teeth extracted (one normal and one wisdom) just 2 days before the #AIFWSS17 was to start. Now I’m left with stitches in my mouth, and the look of a total grumpy face because I can’t smile properly or even talk too much – no food or alcohol can also be consumed either (only soft and cold foods and a diet of antibiotics and painkillers). But it was one those things that I had been delaying for over 8 months and if I hadn’t gotten it done when I did, I would have had to suffer another 8 because I just cannot get myself to visit a dentist. So if you see me at Fashion Week and I don’t smile back at you or smile really weird, you’ll know why.Moving on from my dreary dental story, I can ofcourse have all the fun I want to with my clothes. Max Fashion can also be found on Facebook | Twitter | Instagram | Stay connected with me over Facebook | Twitter | Instagram | Pinterest | Snapchat<*client>For people belonging to/working in the fashion & textile industry, fashion week is one of THE most major events of the year (twice, four times, maybe more – depending on which ones are your priority). The Amazon India Fashion Week Spring Summer ’17 is taking place from October 12th to 16th and the consecutive 5 days of back to back runway shows that never start on time, travelling to the venue and back everyday, attending after-parties, visiting designer stalls, clicking photographs, getting clicked, networking, meeting people, selling yourself or your art and perhaps managing to grab a bite somewhere in the middle, can be nothing less than a harrowing ordeal – however essential and glamorous we may project it to be. And it is of the utmost importance to be prepared for it before hand. It always helps to mark out the shows that you want to attend thanks to the schedule that gets announced and chalk out an itinerary for yourself if you’re going to be a part of the action and want to look alive while doing it. I always start out with spectacular energy when the schedule gets announced, going full steam with excitement and by the second day of fashion week I’m always mentally whispering to myself “I’m so done”. Ofcourse I still go on and power through all days making it look fabulous on my instagram account. And while I don’t want to outright whine about the fashion week (it is ofcourse one of the best ways for me to network, collaborate with brands and put myself out there and I feel extremely great that I get to be a part of it), there are a few things I always make sure I’m carrying with me during this time. I am sharing my ‘Fashion Week’ essentials that I will be carrying on me all 5 days of the Amazon India Fashion Week. I am sharing my ‘Fashion Week’ essentials that I will be carrying on me all 5 days of the Amazon India Fashion Week. Here’s a look:            For people belonging to/working in the fashion & textile industry, fashion week is one of THE most major events of the year (twice, four times, maybe more – depending on which ones are your priority). The Amazon India Fashion Week Spring Summer ’17 is taking place from October 12th to 16th and the consecutive 5 days of back to back runway shows that never start on time, travelling to the venue and back everyday, attending after-parties, visiting designer stalls, clicking photographs, getting clicked, networking, meeting people, selling yourself or your art and perhaps managing to grab a bite somewhere in the middle, can be nothing less than a harrowing ordeal – however essential and glamorous we may project it to be. And it is of the utmost importance to be prepared for it before hand. It always helps to mark out the shows that you want to attend thanks to the schedule that gets announced and chalk out an itinerary for yourself if you’re going to be a part of the action and want to look alive while doing it. I always start out with spectacular energy when the schedule gets announced, going full steam with excitement and by the second day of fashion week I’m always mentally whispering to myself “I’m so done”. Ofcourse I still go on and power through all days making it look fabulous on my instagram account. And while I don’t want to outright whine about the fashion week (it is ofcourse one of the best ways for me to network, collaborate with brands and put myself out there and I feel extremely great that I get to be a part of it), there are a few things I always make sure I’m carrying with me during this time. This season is all about festivities, celebrations, Diwali, Navratri, card parties, indulgence and looking your ethnic best! While sarees and anarkalis look lovely and are evergreen styles, it is always nice to mix up your look a little bit, try a bit of fusion perhaps or just wear the same things in a different manner. The India Modern Festive Store & Fashion Jewellery Store by Amazon Fashion are great places to start building your festive looks for the season. Not only are they specially curated towards festive & ethnic wear – having lehenga cholis, anarkali suits, kurtis, bridal lehengas, sarees and all kinds of jewellery that is easy on the pockets, but it is literally a one-stop-shop for creating endless combinations of lovely outfits that can be delivered quicker than you can say ‘Happy Diwali’! The Amazon Fashion Jewellery Store houses brands like Bbling, Azotique, Aquamarine, Amrita Singh, Malaga, Zariin, and Valiyan by Nitya, etc.For this festive look I decided to try something a bit different from what I usually wear during this season. My entire look has been picked out from Amazon Fashion. I have paired a beautiful light Dabu printed Chanderi Kurta with a royal blue silk maxi skirt and a silk scarf to balance things out and add just a slight bit of sheen to the outfit. From the Amazon Fashion Jewellery Store I picked out a traditional cocktail ring and crystal earrings in the same color palette. The look is finished off by champagne leather heels by Clarks and an embellished clutch. You can find links to each and every product towards the end of the blog post.It’s a very comfortable, breezy and perfectly festive outfit that is ideal for cocktail parties, card-parties when you know the night will last long and even for any day time festivities. It is equally modern I feel with just the right hint of ethnic to it. Mom will be proud! And then it was time.The moment I saw the drones I knew what this was going to be – a real flying fashion show. Life size mannequins wearing looks from the Wills Lifestyle AW16 collection were hung onto the drones and flown back and forth along the up-in-the-air runway over our heads! This was insane! I have never seen anything quite like this before and for that I’m super glad I was invited by Wills! Here are some pics from the flying fashion show. And now I have the perfect partner to carry me through the day – to reinvent my obsession: The new HP Spectre. Being anything but ordinary, the Spectre is not only the world’s thinnest laptop but also comes in the most delicious colorway of black and gold, the black bordering on a classy ash. It lends a sleek, empowering and indulgent element to even the most non-glamorous parts of my work like replying to my emails first thing in the morning. Heck it even makes me seem good in my bathrobe on the bed! Extremely light to carry around all day, jump from one shoot to a quick lunch to my favorite part of the evening – wearing some fabulous clothes and heading out for drinks. My HP Spectre is always within reach because you never know when that exciting new project lands up in my inbox or a particularly important client needs an urgent update. It really is true – the obsession never stops! Enjoy some pics of me through the day.The mornings are all about the most important things I’m crazy about – coffee, some quality time with my love and diving into work emails while I’m still in bed. For me, my emails bring the promise of new, exciting work everyday which is why I obsess so much over them.                                     It’s then time to get dressed, head out for a quick outfit shoot so that I can share my personal style and fashion inspirations with my readers – YOU! Followed by a lunch where I re-check my emails once again, catch up on some editing and drafting of posts on the blog and maybe surf a few websites if I have the time. Days are usually kept casual with an extra formal layer for meetings etc. Like this Burberry dress and trench coat. HP can also be found on Facebook | Twitter | Instagram | Stay connected with me over Facebook | Twitter | Instagram | Pinterest | Snapchat{ *client }Lately I have been so focussed on work and building the blog and it’s reach that I haven’t had the time to pay attention to myself, my body, my mind and their needs. Sure I mostly eat healthy and manage to do Yoga here and there but I could see a steady decline even in the time I was investing in my Yoga. My mind was always switched on and it takes just about a second to switch on the screen of your cellphone and or laptop. I could feel a certain stress building up, my shoulders being tight and in pain all the time and me being bored! Bored! I have never been bored before – I always know how to keep myself entertained even if I’m alone – and no, not with watching tv or surfing the web but with my own damn mind and imagination. I was reminiscing about days when I was broke, had no work but had fabulous days, knew how to have a good time and keep myself entertained and generally feel really good about life. And what bothered me the most was the amount of time my mind and eyes were spending thinking about and looking at work, the screen and the stress in my shoulders. Which is why I am happy to report that I have joined a Yoga class! I’ve been just thrice in my first week and I already feel the change. Not once have my shoulders bothered me with any pain or tightness of muscles, I have about 2 hours everyday apart from my sleep time where I don’t even get the chance to look at any sort of screen and think about anything at all. Really happy I made the decision because for the longest time I felt that I could take care of myself by myself, doing yoga at home etc. But sometimes you need help from outside so that you can get better at self-love. The class will also hopefully bring in some much needed regimen to my hours. Another thing I have done is put my phone on do-not-disturb. No phone calls. It’s so freeing to not be such a slave to that stupid thing. A bit of sportiness added by the stripes on the pants and glasses to make me look serious  My outfit is all from Benetton.Lately I have been so focussed on work and building the blog and it’s reach that I haven’t had the time to pay attention to myself, my body, my mind and their needs. Sure I mostly eat healthy and manage to do Yoga here and there but I could see a steady decline even in the time I was investing in my Yoga. My mind was always switched on and it takes just about a second to switch on the screen of your cellphone and or laptop. I could feel a certain stress building up, my shoulders being tight and in pain all the time and me being bored! Bored! I have never been bored before – I always know how to keep myself entertained even if I’m alone – and no, not with watching tv or surfing the web but with my own damn mind and imagination. I was reminiscing about days when I was broke, had no work but had fabulous days, knew how to have a good time and keep myself entertained and generally feel really good about life. And what bothered me the most was the amount of time my mind and eyes were spending thinking about and looking at work, the screen and the stress in my shoulders. Which is why I am happy to report that I have joined a Yoga class! I’ve been just thrice in my first week and I already feel the change. Not once have my shoulders bothered me with any pain or tightness of muscles, I have about 2 hours everyday apart from my sleep time where I don’t even get the chance to look at any sort of screen and think about anything at all. Really happy I made the decision because for the longest time I felt that I could take care of myself by myself, doing yoga at home etc. But sometimes you need help from outside so that you can get better at self-love. The class will also hopefully bring in some much needed regimen to my hours. Another thing I have done is put my phone on do-not-disturb. No phone calls. It’s so freeing to not be such a slave to that stupid thing.       And obviously no, I’m not saying that yoga can solve everyone’s problems but taking out time for yourself always helps build a stronger relationship with yourself which is THE most important relationship EVER. It’s a mix of casual/nerd/chic and the splatter print on the cardi really gives it an element of fun. A bit of sportiness added by the stripes on the pants and glasses to make me look serious  My outfit is all from Benetton.                                                                              Lately I have been so focussed on work and building the blog and it’s reach that I haven’t had the time to pay attention to myself, my body, my mind and their needs. Sure I mostly eat healthy and manage to do Yoga here and there but I could see a steady decline even in the time I was investing in my Yoga. My mind was always switched on and it takes just about a second to switch on the screen of your cellphone and or laptop. I could feel a certain stress building up, my shoulders being tight and in pain all the time and me being bored! Bored! I have never been bored before – I always know how to keep myself entertained even if I’m alone – and no, not with watching tv or surfing the web but with my own damn mind and imagination. I was reminiscing about days when I was broke, had no work but had fabulous days, knew how to have a good time and keep myself entertained and generally feel really good about life. And what bothered me the most was the amount of time my mind and eyes were spending thinking about and looking at work, the screen and the stress in my shoulders. Which is why I am happy to report that I have joined a Yoga class! I’ve been just thrice in my first week and I already feel the change. Not once have my shoulders bothered me with any pain or tightness of muscles, I have about 2 hours everyday apart from my sleep time where I don’t even get the chance to look at any sort of screen and think about anything at all. Really happy I made the decision because for the longest time I felt that I could take care of myself by myself, doing yoga at home etc. But sometimes you need help from outside so that you can get better at self-love. The class will also hopefully bring in some much needed regimen to my hours. Another thing I have done is put my phone on do-not-disturb. No phone calls. It’s so freeing to not be such a slave to that stupid thing.       And obviously no, I’m not saying that yoga can solve everyone’s problems but taking out time for yourself always helps build a stronger relationship with yourself which is THE most important relationship EVER. Dinner was at Yuan, the pan-Asian restaurant at The Atlantis. No visit is complete here without trying the ‘Chocolate Rocks’ dessert.             Post dinner walk on the beach gives you great views of the hotel.       Next day we took a ride on the Palm Monorail which took us from The Atlantis along the trunk of the Palm Jumeirah. We even got to see the Atlantis in all it’s glory in the day-time.                   We were driven all around Dubai courtesy Arabian Adventures and Partha has so much knowledge of Dubai that you can literally ask him any question & he will have an answer ready. Discovering Dubai with Arabian Adventures was really a highlight of our entire trip. Roamed around in this car on all 4 days.             Last week, Naina & I returned from our fantastic and action packed 4 day trip to Dubai with Emirates Holidays. The 4 days passed us by in the blink of an eye – we had so many wonderful experiences, roamed around so much, ate such fabulous food and visited some of the best hotels & places in Dubai. Yet we managed to cover just the tip of the scratch on the surface of this larger-than-life city called Dubai. The thing that boggles my mind the most however, is the incredible way Dubai had literally been built out of nothing but sand, sheer determination and ofcourse money. I remember saying to Naina how usually across the world and history one finds that man moves to areas with water and trees but in the case of Dubai, it’s the water and the trees that have moved where man is present, quite literally!This post is a collection of our entire Dubai experience – the things we did, places we visited and our experiences. It is actually quite perfect as an itinerary for someone planning to visit Dubai for 4-6 days. Ofcourse another great incentive for a visit right now would be the Dubai Summer Surprises for the shopaholics. It’s a long post with lots of photographs because we did so much. Hope you have fun going through it!Checked into The Atlantis. Naina & I had our own separate suites which were nothing less than amazing!             Stunning views from my room. I remember saying to Naina how usually across the world and history one finds that man moves to areas with water and trees but in the case of Dubai, it’s the water and the trees that have moved where man is present, quite literally!This post is a collection of our entire Dubai experience – the things we did, places we visited and our experiences. It is actually quite perfect as an itinerary for someone planning to visit Dubai for 4-6 days. Ofcourse another great incentive for a visit right now would be the Dubai Summer Surprises for the shopaholics. It’s a long post with lots of photographs because we did so much. Hope you have fun going through it!Checked into The Atlantis. Naina & I had our own separate suites which were nothing less than amazing!             Stunning views from my room.             The lobby of the hotel has a gigantic glass sculpture.       A visit to the Lost Chambers Aquarium is a must! So many wondrous sea creatures to see and discover. My favorite to watch were the jellyfish. They even have cushions and spreads laid out for you to spend hours observing the fish pass you by.       Dinner was at Yuan, the pan-Asian restaurant at The Atlantis. No visit is complete here without trying the ‘Chocolate Rocks’ dessert.             Post dinner walk on the beach gives you great views of the hotel.       Next day we took a ride on the Palm Monorail which took us from The Atlantis along the trunk of the Palm Jumeirah. We even got to see the Atlantis in all it’s glory in the day-time.                   We were driven all around Dubai courtesy Arabian Adventures and Partha has so much knowledge of Dubai that you can literally ask him any question & he will have an answer ready. Discovering Dubai with Arabian Adventures was really a highlight of our entire trip. Roamed around in this car on all 4 days.             After this we visited At The Top, Burj Khalifa (the tallest building in the world). With 160 storeys, we went up to At The Top SKY which is level 148. They have a classy lounge where we were served refreshments and even an outdoors observation deck if you want to venture into the heat. The views were ofcourse the best you can get.                                The view of th ebuilding when you are back on solid ground.       Lunch was at The Palace Downtown Dubai. They have a lovely Arabic lunch buffet that you mustn’t miss.                   After this we headed to The Dubai Mall where the girls at Bloomingdale’s Dubai had planned a pampering time for the both of us. They took us through their personal shopping experience where they had already gone through our instagram accounts and picked out looks, shoes, bags & accessories that they thought we’d love (which ofcourse we did!). Even though I don’t have a particular style that I stick to, they somehow got it and I loved the kind of stuff they had laid out for me. I went for a total Alice + Olivia look with Stella McCartney shoes. After this we were whisked away to get hair & makeup done. The lobby of the hotel has a gigantic glass sculpture.       A visit to the Lost Chambers Aquarium is a must! So many wondrous sea creatures to see and discover. My favorite to watch were the jellyfish. They even have cushions and spreads laid out for you to spend hours observing the fish pass you by.       Dinner was at Yuan, the pan-Asian restaurant at The Atlantis. No visit is complete here without trying the ‘Chocolate Rocks’ dessert. We even got to see the Atlantis in all it’s glory in the day-time.                   We were driven all around Dubai courtesy Arabian Adventures and Partha has so much knowledge of Dubai that you can literally ask him any question & he will have an answer ready. Discovering Dubai with Arabian Adventures was really a highlight of our entire trip. Roamed around in this car on all 4 days.             After this we visited At The Top, Burj Khalifa (the tallest building in the world). With 160 storeys, we went up to At The Top SKY which is level 148. They have a classy lounge where we were served refreshments and even an outdoors observation deck if you want to venture into the heat. The views were ofcourse the best you can get.                                The view of th ebuilding when you are back on solid ground.       Lunch was at The Palace Downtown Dubai. They have a lovely Arabic lunch buffet that you mustn’t miss.                   After this we headed to The Dubai Mall where the girls at Bloomingdale’s Dubai had planned a pampering time for the both of us. They took us through their personal shopping experience where they had already gone through our instagram accounts and picked out looks, shoes, bags & accessories that they thought we’d love (which ofcourse we did!). Even though I don’t have a particular style that I stick to, they somehow got it and I loved the kind of stuff they had laid out for me. I went for a total Alice + Olivia look with Stella McCartney shoes. After this we were whisked away to get hair & makeup done. Then onto some yummy cupcakes at the Magnolia Bakery and finally a tour of their ‘Home Section’                         A quick stopover at the St. Regis Dubai for some ‘Golden Marys’ (the more charming sister of the Bloody Mary)             Our dinner was with the Bateaux Dubai Cruises. A beautiful 2 hour long cruise over the Dubai Creek. Great food and some soothing night views of Dubai over the sparkling waters. Another beautiful experience.                   Next day, after a much needed Swedish massage at the Shiqui Spa at the Atlantis, we checked out and went on to explore the Burj Al Arab, which has been voted the world’s most luxurious hotel many times over. We ate lunch at their new restaurant ‘Scape’. Co-incidentally my Missoni dress looked like a part of the interiors at Burj Al Arab and I was almost camouflaging. For lunch I ate crab burgers. Super stuff.                    Scape is on the left in blue.             After lunch we checked into Taj, Dubai for the remaining of our trip. Our room was on the 34th floor and we had a fabulous view of the Burj Khalifa from it!                                      View of Dubai from our room at night.             Last week, Naina & I returned from our fantastic and action packed 4 day trip to Dubai with Emirates Holidays. The 4 days passed us by in the blink of an eye – we had so many wonderful experiences, roamed around so much, ate such fabulous food and visited some of the best hotels & places in Dubai. Yet we managed to cover just the tip of the scratch on the surface of this larger-than-life city called Dubai. The thing that boggles my mind the most however, is the incredible way Dubai had literally been built out of nothing but sand, sheer determination and ofcourse money. I remember saying to Naina how usually across the world and history one finds that man moves to areas with water and trees but in the case of Dubai, it’s the water and the trees that have moved where man is present, quite literally!This post is a collection of our entire Dubai experience – the things we did, places we visited and our experiences. It is actually quite perfect as an itinerary for someone planning to visit Dubai for 4-6 days. Last week, Naina & I returned from our fantastic and action packed 4 day trip to Dubai with Emirates Holidays. The 4 days passed us by in the blink of an eye – we had so many wonderful experiences, roamed around so much, ate such fabulous food and visited some of the best hotels & places in Dubai. Yet we managed to cover just the tip of the scratch on the surface of this larger-than-life city called Dubai. The thing that boggles my mind the most however, is the incredible way Dubai had literally been built out of nothing but sand, sheer determination and ofcourse money. I remember saying to Naina how usually across the world and history one finds that man moves to areas with water and trees but in the case of Dubai, it’s the water and the trees that have moved where man is present, quite literally!This post is a collection of our entire Dubai experience – the things we did, places we visited and our experiences. It is actually quite perfect as an itinerary for someone planning to visit Dubai for 4-6 days. Ofcourse another great incentive for a visit right now would be the Dubai Summer Surprises for the shopaholics. It’s a long post with lots of photographs because we did so much. Hope you have fun going through it!Checked into The Atlantis. Naina & I had our own separate suites which were nothing less than amazing!             Stunning views from my room.             The lobby of the hotel has a gigantic glass sculpture.       A visit to the Lost Chambers Aquarium is a must! So many wondrous sea creatures to see and discover. My favorite to watch were the jellyfish. They even have cushions and spreads laid out for you to spend hours observing the fish pass you by.       Dinner was at Yuan, the pan-Asian restaurant at The Atlantis. No visit is complete here without trying the ‘Chocolate Rocks’ dessert.             Post dinner walk on the beach gives you great views of the hotel.       Next day we took a ride on the Palm Monorail which took us from The Atlantis along the trunk of the Palm Jumeirah. We even got to see the Atlantis in all it’s glory in the day-time.                   We were driven all around Dubai courtesy Arabian Adventures and Partha has so much knowledge of Dubai that you can literally ask him any question & he will have an answer ready. Discovering Dubai with Arabian Adventures was really a highlight of our entire trip. Roamed around in this car on all 4 days.             After this we visited At The Top, Burj Khalifa (the tallest building in the world). With 160 storeys, we went up to At The Top SKY which is level 148. They have a classy lounge where we were served refreshments and even an outdoors observation deck if you want to venture into the heat. The views were ofcourse the best you can get.                                The view of th ebuilding when you are back on solid ground.       Lunch was at The Palace Downtown Dubai. They have a lovely Arabic lunch buffet that you mustn’t miss.                   After this we headed to The Dubai Mall where the girls at Bloomingdale’s Dubai had planned a pampering time for the both of us. They took us through their personal shopping experience where they had already gone through our instagram accounts and picked out looks, shoes, bags & accessories that they thought we’d love (which ofcourse we did!). Even though I don’t have a particular style that I stick to, they somehow got it and I loved the kind of stuff they had laid out for me. I went for a total Alice + Olivia look with Stella McCartney shoes. After this we were whisked away to get hair & makeup done. Then onto some yummy cupcakes at the Magnolia Bakery and finally a tour of their ‘Home Section’                         A quick stopover at the St. Regis Dubai for some ‘Golden Marys’ (the more charming sister of the Bloody Mary)             Our dinner was with the Bateaux Dubai Cruises. A beautiful 2 hour long cruise over the Dubai Creek. Great food and some soothing night views of Dubai over the sparkling waters. Another beautiful experience.                   Next day, after a much needed Swedish massage at the Shiqui Spa at the Atlantis, we checked out and went on to explore the Burj Al Arab, which has been voted the world’s most luxurious hotel many times over. We ate lunch at their new restaurant ‘Scape’. Co-incidentally my Missoni dress looked like a part of the interiors at Burj Al Arab and I was almost camouflaging. For lunch I ate crab burgers. Super stuff.                    Scape is on the left in blue.             After lunch we checked into Taj, Dubai for the remaining of our trip. Our room was on the 34th floor and we had a fabulous view of the Burj Khalifa from it!                                      View of Dubai from our room at night.             Next day was breakfast at Tesoro, Taj, Dubai.       After breakfast, I caught up with some work and for lunch we headed out to Palazzo Versace Dubai for lunch at Vanitas, their Italian restaurant. Their burrata salad is something you will never be able to get out of your head. I followed that up with some absolutely stunning lamb. The hotel’s interiors are, for lack of a better word, very Versace. And because I was in a specially fun mood, I decide to wear a Versace shirt to my visit here. Yes, I’m that person!              Spot me!                   After lunch we headed on to another very exciting experience – Heli Dubai. It is actually quite perfect as an itinerary for someone planning to visit Dubai for 4-6 days. Ofcourse another great incentive for a visit right now would be the Dubai Summer Surprises for the shopaholics. It’s a long post with lots of photographs because we did so much. Hope you have fun going through it!Checked into The Atlantis. Naina & I had our own separate suites which were nothing less than amazing!             Stunning views from my room.             The lobby of the hotel has a gigantic glass sculpture.       A visit to the Lost Chambers Aquarium is a must! So many wondrous sea creatures to see and discover. My favorite to watch were the jellyfish. They even have cushions and spreads laid out for you to spend hours observing the fish pass you by.       Dinner was at Yuan, the pan-Asian restaurant at The Atlantis. No visit is complete here without trying the ‘Chocolate Rocks’ dessert.             Post dinner walk on the beach gives you great views of the hotel.       Next day we took a ride on the Palm Monorail which took us from The Atlantis along the trunk of the Palm Jumeirah. We even got to see the Atlantis in all it’s glory in the day-time.                   We were driven all around Dubai courtesy Arabian Adventures and Partha has so much knowledge of Dubai that you can literally ask him any question & he will have an answer ready. Discovering Dubai with Arabian Adventures was really a highlight of our entire trip. Roamed around in this car on all 4 days.             After this we visited At The Top, Burj Khalifa (the tallest building in the world). With 160 storeys, we went up to At The Top SKY which is level 148. They have a classy lounge where we were served refreshments and even an outdoors observation deck if you want to venture into the heat. The views were ofcourse the best you can get.                                The view of th ebuilding when you are back on solid ground.       Lunch was at The Palace Downtown Dubai. They have a lovely Arabic lunch buffet that you mustn’t miss.                   After this we headed to The Dubai Mall where the girls at Bloomingdale’s Dubai had planned a pampering time for the both of us. They took us through their personal shopping experience where they had already gone through our instagram accounts and picked out looks, shoes, bags & accessories that they thought we’d love (which ofcourse we did!). Even though I don’t have a particular style that I stick to, they somehow got it and I loved the kind of stuff they had laid out for me. I went for a total Alice + Olivia look with Stella McCartney shoes. After this we were whisked away to get hair & makeup done. Then onto some yummy cupcakes at the Magnolia Bakery and finally a tour of their ‘Home Section’                         A quick stopover at the St. Regis Dubai for some ‘Golden Marys’ (the more charming sister of the Bloody Mary)             Our dinner was with the Bateaux Dubai Cruises. A beautiful 2 hour long cruise over the Dubai Creek. Great food and some soothing night views of Dubai over the sparkling waters. Another beautiful experience.                   Next day, after a much needed Swedish massage at the Shiqui Spa at the Atlantis, we checked out and went on to explore the Burj Al Arab, which has been voted the world’s most luxurious hotel many times over. We ate lunch at their new restaurant ‘Scape’. Co-incidentally my Missoni dress looked like a part of the interiors at Burj Al Arab and I was almost camouflaging. For lunch I ate crab burgers. Super stuff.                    Scape is on the left in blue.             After lunch we checked into Taj, Dubai for the remaining of our trip. Our room was on the 34th floor and we had a fabulous view of the Burj Khalifa from it!                                      View of Dubai from our room at night.             Next day was breakfast at Tesoro, Taj, Dubai.       After breakfast, I caught up with some work and for lunch we headed out to Palazzo Versace Dubai for lunch at Vanitas, their Italian restaurant. Their burrata salad is something you will never be able to get out of your head. I followed that up with some absolutely stunning lamb. The hotel’s interiors are, for lack of a better word, very Versace. And because I was in a specially fun mood, I decide to wear a Versace shirt to my visit here. Yes, I’m that person!              Spot me!                   After lunch we headed on to another very exciting experience – Heli Dubai. A 17 minute long helicopter ride over Dubai where we flew up till the tip of the Palm Jumeirah, even spotted our previous hotel Atlantis and headed back. What fun!                          Also spotted the Burj Al Arab.       Next day was in room breakfast at Taj Dubai. After a few hours I went in for the 45 minute ‘Champi’ massage and I highly recommend it! Then onto packing up our stuff, checking out and flying back to India. Thank you Emirates Holidays for this amazing adventure and also the business class travel! I am happy to share that this year the British Council has commissioned a series of films using Shakespeare’s works as inspiration as part of Shakespeare Lives 2016; an unprecedented global programme celebrating William Shakespeare’s work and his influence on culture, education and society on the 400th anniversary of his death.      They have recently released their sixth short film ‘Come To Me’, which is a blues song that takes inspiration from the songs found in As You Like It, and explores the lifecycle of a romantic relationship reflected in the changing seasons. Director Prasanna Puwanarajah, and musician Anjana Vasan, who is currently playing the role of Hermia in A Midsummer Night’s Dream at The Globe in London, present a musical triptych, which takes the audience on an emotional journey charting the beginning of a relationship in spring time through to its disintegration post winter. It begins with a pleasant and lovely note of fresh love and leans towards a haunting end. You must give it a listen. I had heard from a lot of people about how amazing Nusa Dua is. After a day or two of exploring our surroundings near The Grand Nikko Bali we decided to drive further out and see more, which is how we actually stumbled upon this extremely well maintained, chic and beautiful area of Nusa Dua that is gated and guarded at all points of entry and the guards even ask you where you are headed sometimes. There are a bunch of tourist spots to check out but mostly it’s a collective effort of all the high-end hotels that reside within this lovely locality called the Nusa Dua BTDC complex – Bali Tourism Development Corporation which is a state owned enterprise. Very impressive, clean and safe. You MUST visit the Waterblow – the few days we were there it was shut to the public because of random wave warnings. But you can explore the area, find your own little nook and get to some rock formations from where you will get a spectacular display of the waterblow or the waves crashing against the rocks. It’s pretty amazing. Don’t forget to wear your shoes though – I went wearing my flip flops and the rocks can get quite jagged so I did sort of lose my balance and leaned against a big cactus with my hands. Was picking out thorns from my palm for the next 10 minutes. #truestory. There are a whole lot of restaurants and even a large shopping complex called ‘Bali Collection’. This place is ideal for families with kids because it’s safe, less crowded and very well maintained – the roads are gorgeous! Very impressive, clean and safe. You MUST visit the Waterblow – the few days we were there it was shut to the public because of random wave warnings. But you can explore the area, find your own little nook and get to some rock formations from where you will get a spectacular display of the waterblow or the waves crashing against the rocks. It’s pretty amazing. Don’t forget to wear your shoes though – I went wearing my flip flops and the rocks can get quite jagged so I did sort of lose my balance and leaned against a big cactus with my hands. Was picking out thorns from my palm for the next 10 minutes. #truestory. There are a whole lot of restaurants and even a large shopping complex called ‘Bali Collection’. This place is ideal for families with kids because it’s safe, less crowded and very well maintained – the roads are gorgeous! I’m wearing a beautiful boho-colorful Hemant & Nandita dress and carrying the luscious handcrafted leather bag by Hidesign from their Atelier Collection that is launching soon! Over 17,000,000 students—most from low-income communities, and many in disaster-stricken areas—have received books, art supplies, field trips, technology, and other resources that they need to learn.      The new Delight Automatic Collection by Frédérique Constant supports this charitable cause and with each watch sold $50 are contributed to directly support innovative, impactful and lasting charity organisations around the world, helping women and children in particular. The new Frédérique Constant Delight Collection has been designed with the perfect combination of elegance, form, and slenderness, its irresistible cocktail representing the apex in feminine style. From the wonderfully slim case, to the slender hands, everything about this design underlines the Frédérique Constant philosophy of accessible luxury. It’s almost perfect when you get to indulge in luxury and charity at the same time! Pantai really just means beach so this post is about our day at Melasti Beach right in the southern extreme of Bali. The beach in itself is a tiny one with pockets of water in which you can chill, no waves to disturb you. As you go further inside the water there is a natural barrier of rocks which keeps the waves from reaching the shore. And even further in from there are waves you would not want to get close to unless you surf. There are a couple of local shacks selling cold beverages, Bintangs, coconut waters and tid-bits to eat. More often than not you will find a wedding shoot happening as you approach the beach because of the spectacular views that it has to offer. We did too! As you go further inside the water there is a natural barrier of rocks which keeps the waves from reaching the shore. And even further in from there are waves you would not want to get close to unless you surf. There are a couple of local shacks selling cold beverages, Bintangs, coconut waters and tid-bits to eat. More often than not you will find a wedding shoot happening as you approach the beach because of the spectacular views that it has to offer. We did too! And naturally, I couldn’t let the opportunity go to waste so I did a quick shoot in the most stunning dress by AM:PM by Ankur & Priyanka Modi from their Spring/Summer ’16 collection.      I reckon not many people know about this beach which is why we only saw locals at the beach. No tourists! It is located on the west coast of South Kuta and definitely a very picturesque beach that will be a perfect setting for a day of beach-bumming. While, like most beaches in Bali, Padang Padang is not ideal for swimming, you can try and venture into the rocky beach at your own pace. There is lots of natural shade because of the trees and no sun-beds or umbrellas put out for anyone. So you will need to carry your beach spread, lots of sunscreen, a book to keep you busy and some music although most of the times I love how the sound of the waves, roasting in the sun and the salt water seem to put me to sleep like a baby. There are a couple of local shacks with ice-cold Bintangs and fresh young coconuts. No pesky sellers bothering you with selling trinkets. It is also a lovely long beach to take a walk on. It is located on the west coast of South Kuta and definitely a very picturesque beach that will be a perfect setting for a day of beach-bumming. While, like most beaches in Bali, Padang Padang is not ideal for swimming, you can try and venture into the rocky beach at your own pace. There is lots of natural shade because of the trees and no sun-beds or umbrellas put out for anyone. So you will need to carry your beach spread, lots of sunscreen, a book to keep you busy and some music although most of the times I love how the sound of the waves, roasting in the sun and the salt water seem to put me to sleep like a baby. There are a couple of local shacks with ice-cold Bintangs and fresh young coconuts. No pesky sellers bothering you with selling trinkets. It is also a lovely long beach to take a walk on.       Since we were staying on the east coast of South Kuta, it was about a 30 minute ride for us on the two-wheeler and I made sure to cover up with a beautiful outfit by Three Clothing by Pallavi Dhyani and my favorite jewelry of the season from Zariin – there is something so soothing and feminine about these dusty pink Rhodochrosite pieces I’m wearing. Zariin has also come up with an exciting new trunk concept to help you with your holiday shopping. Classic and versatile, I know I will be using this jewelry for lots and lots of more vacations to come! We rode on our two-wheeler from the sunny sea level and right into the cloudy, moody hills with magnificent views for lunch and decided to stop on the way to have some fresh coconut water smack in the middle of a rice-field. This is what happiness is made of (atleast in my world).      The local shack owner looked at my pineapple printed polo tee from Amazon and asked me twice if I was sure I wanted coconut water and not pineapple. Haah! Here are some pics from the simple, sweet and blissful day.                                          Also love my new Urmi clutch handmade from recycled materials! The JW Marriott at Aerocity, New Delhi has recently appointed Chef Vivek Bhatt as their new Executive Chef and I was super excited to be invited for lunch and some time with the Chef recently. Not only did Chef Vivek Bhatt have some of his signature dishes prepared for us for lunch, he graciously spent a good 2 hours chatting with us and even sat down to have a bite during lunch. And he is a busy man! So it was extra special that he took out time for us. Chef has been all over the world with nearly 2 decades of experience in the hospitality industry and his main responsibilities at JW Marriott now  are grooming and development of the culinary team members of the hotel; menu curation and product development; and ensuring highest standards in hygiene and quality of the food served at the hotel.. Phew!      Moving on to lunch, before I mention anything else I will say this – If there is ONE thing you eat at JW Marriott, (provided you are a non-vegetarian, duh) it HAS to be the ‘Raan-e-parda’ by Chef Vivek. And nothing else. My mind, tastebuds and soul were blown away by this dish which is one of Chef’s favorites too! It is basically tender lamb leg wrapped inside ‘Sheermal’ dough and cooked/baked over 6 hours to produce the most perfect and unique lamb dish I have ever laid my eyes on. You don’t really need any sort of rice or Indian bread with this because it’s a complete package. Be warned: You WILL overeat. The rest of the dishes that Chef had prepared for us were: Machli Zameendoz(another unique preparation, more about it later in the post), Murgh ki chaap, Goolar kebab, Chowk ki tikki, Vilaiti Subz jalfrazi, Dal Makhani and for dessert –  Shahi Tukhra.The JW Marriott at Aerocity, New Delhi has recently appointed Chef Vivek Bhatt as their new Executive Chef and I was super excited to be invited for lunch and some time with the Chef recently. Not only did Chef Vivek Bhatt have some of his signature dishes prepared for us for lunch, he graciously spent a good 2 hours chatting with us and even sat down to have a bite during lunch. And he is a busy man! So it was extra special that he took out time for us. Chef has been all over the world with nearly 2 decades of experience in the hospitality industry and his main responsibilities at JW Marriott now  are grooming and development of the culinary team members of the hotel; menu curation and product development; and ensuring highest standards in hygiene and quality of the food served at the hotel.. Phew!      Moving on to lunch, before I mention anything else I will say this – If there is ONE thing you eat at JW Marriott, (provided you are a non-vegetarian, duh) it HAS to be the ‘Raan-e-parda’ by Chef Vivek. And nothing else. My mind, tastebuds and soul were blown away by this dish which is one of Chef’s favorites too! It is basically tender lamb leg wrapped inside ‘Sheermal’ dough and cooked/baked over 6 hours to produce the most perfect and unique lamb dish I have ever laid my eyes on. You don’t really need any sort of rice or Indian bread with this because it’s a complete package. Be warned: You WILL overeat. The rest of the dishes that Chef had prepared for us were: Machli Zameendoz(another unique preparation, more about it later in the post), Murgh ki chaap, Goolar kebab, Chowk ki tikki, Vilaiti Subz jalfrazi, Dal Makhani and for dessert –  Shahi Tukhra.We also got a taste of the exotic and my first ever Jamun cocktails along with lunch. Woop woop! Here are pics from lunch at JW Marriott. The rest of the dishes that Chef had prepared for us were: Machli Zameendoz(another unique preparation, more about it later in the post), Murgh ki chaap, Goolar kebab, Chowk ki tikki, Vilaiti Subz jalfrazi, Dal Makhani and for dessert –  Shahi Tukhra.We also got a taste of the exotic and my first ever Jamun cocktails along with lunch. Woop woop! Here are pics from lunch at JW Marriott. Not very many people know about this pretty beach so you will mostly find only the hotel guests and a handful of local fishermen on this beach which makes it perfect for spending a quiet day at the beach. Not very many people know about this pretty beach so you will mostly find only the hotel guests and a handful of local fishermen on this beach which makes it perfect for spending a quiet day at the beach. There is a narrow path that turns towards the beach right next to the entry of The Grand Nikko Bali – it’s easy to miss but very rewarding if you don’t. There is one lone shack called ‘Barefoot Bali’ on the beach that will cater to your needs of chilled beer, coconut water and some really good Mie Goreng. You also won’t be bothered by too many locals trying to sell you stuff. However like most beaches of Bali, this one is rocky too and not ideal for swimming. I carry the scar to prove so.No beach vacation is quite complete unless half my clothes are white and so, I wore my pretty white SBUYS dress along with some gold bling in the form of my Guess watch and some rings. The rest was just water, sand, sun and coconuts! Yay! SBUYS can also be found on Facebook | Twitter | Instagram | Stay connected with me over Facebook | Twitter | Instagram | Pinterest | Snapchat*{ client }Another favorite spot in Bali turned out to be the Nungnung waterfall near Ubud. For reasons unknown it is not as popular as the other waterfalls which adds to its charm since you won’t find big crowds here and you are left to explore the area at your own sweet pace. A quick warning though: there are lots and lots and lots of stairs involved (maybe the reason why it isn’t so popular). So it is not ideal for older aged people. On your way to the waterfall it is mostly climbing down all the stairs so you don’t really feel anything but the way up is a different story. We had to stop a couple of times to catch our breath. Luckily there are gazebo-type hut-lets that have been erected at regular intervals so you can easily find place to sit down, relax and enjoy the views.Another favorite spot in Bali turned out to be the Nungnung waterfall near Ubud. Another favorite spot in Bali turned out to be the Nungnung waterfall near Ubud. For reasons unknown it is not as popular as the other waterfalls which adds to its charm since you won’t find big crowds here and you are left to explore the area at your own sweet pace. A quick warning though: there are lots and lots and lots of stairs involved (maybe the reason why it isn’t so popular). So it is not ideal for older aged people. On your way to the waterfall it is mostly climbing down all the stairs so you don’t really feel anything but the way up is a different story. We had to stop a couple of times to catch our breath. Luckily there are gazebo-type hut-lets that have been erected at regular intervals so you can easily find place to sit down, relax and enjoy the views.      The Nungnung waterfalls are easily found on Google maps and there is no need to stop and ask for directions at any point. We drove from our hotel in Ubud to the waterfalls on our two-wheeler and it took us about 40-50 minutes to reach our destination. Plenty of space to park. You have to purchase an entry ticket of a very nominal amount. Don’t forget to carry a bottle of water for your journey back. It is also a good idea to wear something light, comfortable and which you can take off and put on easily if you intend to take a dip in the water. My cotton shirt dress by ‘Life’ brand from Shoppers Stop was ideal for this.Another favorite spot in Bali turned out to be the Nungnung waterfall near Ubud. A quick warning though: there are lots and lots and lots of stairs involved (maybe the reason why it isn’t so popular). So it is not ideal for older aged people. On your way to the waterfall it is mostly climbing down all the stairs so you don’t really feel anything but the way up is a different story. We had to stop a couple of times to catch our breath. Luckily there are gazebo-type hut-lets that have been erected at regular intervals so you can easily find place to sit down, relax and enjoy the views.      The Nungnung waterfalls are easily found on Google maps and there is no need to stop and ask for directions at any point. We drove from our hotel in Ubud to the waterfalls on our two-wheeler and it took us about 40-50 minutes to reach our destination. Plenty of space to park. You have to purchase an entry ticket of a very nominal amount. Don’t forget to carry a bottle of water for your journey back. It is also a good idea to wear something light, comfortable and which you can take off and put on easily if you intend to take a dip in the water. My cotton shirt dress by ‘Life’ brand from Shoppers Stop was ideal for this.      The waterfall itself is quite magnificent. If you are feeling a bit adventurous you can climb across a few big rocks and boulders and make your way right to the end and even go under the waterfall. There is also space slightly away from the waterfall where you can take a dip into the cool water which is extremely welcoming since the climb down tends to get quite humid and hot. We relaxed in the cool water for around 10 minutes during which we saw about  2 groups of people come and go. Another favorite spot in Bali turned out to be the Nungnung waterfall near Ubud. On your way to the waterfall it is mostly climbing down all the stairs so you don’t really feel anything but the way up is a different story. We had to stop a couple of times to catch our breath. Luckily there are gazebo-type hut-lets that have been erected at regular intervals so you can easily find place to sit down, relax and enjoy the views.      The Nungnung waterfalls are easily found on Google maps and there is no need to stop and ask for directions at any point. We drove from our hotel in Ubud to the waterfalls on our two-wheeler and it took us about 40-50 minutes to reach our destination. Plenty of space to park. You have to purchase an entry ticket of a very nominal amount. Don’t forget to carry a bottle of water for your journey back. It is also a good idea to wear something light, comfortable and which you can take off and put on easily if you intend to take a dip in the water. My cotton shirt dress by ‘Life’ brand from Shoppers Stop was ideal for this.      The waterfall itself is quite magnificent. If you are feeling a bit adventurous you can climb across a few big rocks and boulders and make your way right to the end and even go under the waterfall. There is also space slightly away from the waterfall where you can take a dip into the cool water which is extremely welcoming since the climb down tends to get quite humid and hot. We relaxed in the cool water for around 10 minutes during which we saw about  2 groups of people come and go. Definitely a must-visit for anybody staying in Ubud. You will not be disappointed. Plus it will be a great workout! Here are some pics from our visit. There is no specific entry point to the Tegalalang rice terraces. There are a lot of ‘view-point’ cafes and restaurants lining the edge from where you can view the terraces and enter into them. Since it was so early everything was shut and we went into a restaurant which was giving the promise of the best view in the area. This was after roaming around for a bit and trying to figure out where to actually get into the rice fields from. We also ran into a few other tourists who were facing the same dilemma. If you visit during the day ofcourse you will have to actually sit at a particular cafe or restaurant, pay for something to eat or drink there and then you can proceed further into the rice fields. During peak hours, the local residents also tend to ask you for a small fee if you happen to be crossing through their rice-fields (again, I have only read and heard about this is, I did not personally experience this)We woke up super early for this visit to the iconic rice terraces in Ubud. It was a very quiet narrow road and we landed right into the heart of the rice fields at the base with a tiny stream running across. A beautiful morning spent breathing fresh air and taking in gorgeous views. The sun hadn’t managed to come through by the time we wrapped up and decided to head back to our hotel for some breakfast. Perfect!The rice terraces are definitely a must-see for someone visiting Ubud but I find them to be a bit overrated in my humble opinion.                                           We woke up super early for this visit to the iconic rice terraces in Ubud. For most sight-seeing in Bali I have realized that being early is the quite literally the best policy because places tend to get crowded really quick. So your best bet is to visit as early as possible – not only do you tend to avoid crowds of people in your pics, you also avoid those nagging locals trying to sell you stuff and tours and taxi rides. You have almost the whole place to yourself and can truly explore it at your own pace. We reached the area at around sunrise and since it was early morning it was still cloudy and the sun hadn’t yet come out. Wearing my cute little Oxolloxo dress in solid pastel-mint.      There is no specific entry point to the Tegalalang rice terraces. There are a lot of ‘view-point’ cafes and restaurants lining the edge from where you can view the terraces and enter into them. Since it was so early everything was shut and we went into a restaurant which was giving the promise of the best view in the area. This was after roaming around for a bit and trying to figure out where to actually get into the rice fields from. We also ran into a few other tourists who were facing the same dilemma. If you visit during the day ofcourse you will have to actually sit at a particular cafe or restaurant, pay for something to eat or drink there and then you can proceed further into the rice fields. You tend to learn and explore so much more when you move out of the popular spots, drive off on a whim and discover your own favorite places. Soka beach was one such discovery. It was our longest day on the two wheeler – Bali is a BIG island and you definitely cannot explore it on a bike. To test our limits (more like the limits of our butts) we set out from Seminyak and hit Soka in about 1 hour 40 minutes – OUCHIE! But that wasn’t the end. We spent some time here and moved further to an EVEN better beach – Balian Beach. This one was pure beauty but more on that in another post. But by the end of the day with more than 4 hours spent on the bike, my bum had gone off to sleep (yes that can happen – another discovery I made)I wore a striped look from the fresh new United Colors of Benetton collection in stores because well – a beach vacation is incomplete without a striped outfit. The cotton jersey makes it super comfy and breathable and who doesn’t like crop tops and midi-skirts?!                        I always find it very rewarding to visit the lesser known spots and beaches – they tend to be less crowded (sometimes you have the entire beach to yourself) as well as cleaner and untouched with more authentic shacks and restaurants offering local cuisine – case in point Soka Beach. Stay connected with me over Facebook | Twitter | Instagram | Pinterest | Snapchat<*client>One of my favorite Swiss watchmakers, Longines has recently welcomed Kate Winslet, it’s Ambassador of Elegance to Saint-Imier in Switzerland, where the brand was first created in 1832. Kate, accompanied by Walter von Känel, President of Longines witnessed the production and assembly processes. She also visited the Longines Museum, where she fell in love with a particular watch from the Flagship Collection which the brand has now decided to re-issue during the course of the year. Proceeds of the sales of this watch will go towards the Golden Hat Foundation – a non-profit organization co-founded by Kate Winslet in 2010. The Golden Hat Foundation strives to highlight the capabilities and the immense potential of individuals with autism.One of my favorite Swiss watchmakers, Longines has recently welcomed Kate Winslet, it’s Ambassador of Elegance to Saint-Imier in Switzerland, where the brand was first created in 1832. Kate, accompanied by Walter von Känel, President of Longines witnessed the production and assembly processes. She also visited the Longines Museum, where she fell in love with a particular watch from the Flagship Collection which the brand has now decided to re-issue during the course of the year. Proceeds of the sales of this watch will go towards the Golden Hat Foundation – a non-profit organization co-founded by Kate Winslet in 2010. The Golden Hat Foundation strives to highlight the capabilities and the immense potential of individuals with autism.For the past 6 years, Kate Winslet has been Longines‘ Ambassador of Elegance and Longines’ deeply held values are fully in line with those demonstrated by the actress through the Golden Hat Foundation. The Swiss watchmaker is thrilled to be associated with such a shining example of altruism as Kate Winslet since it has a long tradition of supporting worthy causes. What a lovely, symbiotic and elegant relationship!One of my favorite Swiss watchmakers, Longines has recently welcomed Kate Winslet, it’s Ambassador of Elegance to Saint-Imier in Switzerland, where the brand was first created in 1832. Kate, accompanied by Walter von Känel, President of Longines witnessed the production and assembly processes. She also visited the Longines Museum, where she fell in love with a particular watch from the Flagship Collection which the brand has now decided to re-issue during the course of the year. Proceeds of the sales of this watch will go towards the Golden Hat Foundation – a non-profit organization co-founded by Kate Winslet in 2010. The Golden Hat Foundation strives to highlight the capabilities and the immense potential of individuals with autism.For the past 6 years, Kate Winslet has been Longines‘ Ambassador of Elegance and Longines’ deeply held values are fully in line with those demonstrated by the actress through the Golden Hat Foundation. The Swiss watchmaker is thrilled to be associated with such a shining example of altruism as Kate Winslet since it has a long tradition of supporting worthy causes. What a lovely, symbiotic and elegant relationship!At the end of this eventful day, Kate was eager to meet with Longines employees, who had gathered for the occasion. The actress took the opportunity to say a few words: “I was delighted to learn that Longines is so in touch with its rich history, from which it draws inspiration for creating new works of art that adhere to its values. I am deeply grateful to Longines for the support they have shown for the Golden Hat Foundation, an organization that is dear to my heart, by re-issuing the watch that I have chosen today. It makes me incredibly proud to be able to contribute to raising public awareness of the situation that individuals with autism face. I believe that these individuals will greatly benefit from the possibility of learning to communicate, of receiving academic training and of developing real social relationships.”One of my favorite Swiss watchmakers, Longines has recently welcomed Kate Winslet, it’s Ambassador of Elegance to Saint-Imier in Switzerland, where the brand was first created in 1832.
